newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek depo, forward curves stable, bond yields flat.
newsitem.headline: Greek depo, forward curves stable, bond yields flat.

text.p: Greek depos were stable except for a drop in overnight drachmas and forex forwards in late trade, dealers said.
Bonds were battered early after the auction of five-, seven- and 10-year bonds on July 15, with yields steadying at higher levels, dealers said.
Ecu/drachma was locked in the tight 309.40/60 range and mark/drachma weakened on a firmer ecu/mark, dealers said.
"Depos are holding with the exception of overnight rates, which dipped," a dealer at a private bank said. "Forex forwards are fluctuating narrowly."
Yields of five- seven- and 10-year bonds stabilised after jumping in early dealings on selling by local banks.
"Some players chose to sell their bonds, thinking they would buy them cheaper at the auction," said a bond dealer at a private bank. "The market is quiet.

Greece will seek bids for a further 75 billion drachmas each of five- and seven-year bonds with coupons of 9.2 percent and 8.9 percent respectively, and 120 billion drachmas ($434.5 million) of 8.8 percent, 10-year bonds on July 15, the finance ministry announced late on Thursday.
The five- and seven-year bonds were auctioned for the first time on March 19 and then, bids were re-opened on June 17. The 10-year bonds were auctioned for the first time on June 17.
Greece will also auction 150 billion drachmas of seven-year floating rate notes on July 29.
The mark was quoted at 157.10/20 from Friday's 157.155 fix, the dollar at 276.68/78 drachmas from 276.110 and the ecu at 309.45/55 from 309.50 drachmas.
